metadata.case_name: TSENG TIEN PEI v. CHAN SHUN KWONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: employed in the electronic industry in a skilled supervisory or assistant managerial capacity

injuries.description: whip lash injuries to his neck
source: He suffered what are commonly known as "whip lash" injuries to his neck.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

source: It appears from the evidence of Dr. Hunter that the plaintiff's symptoms are as a result of degenerative changes to his spine

manifestations.description: Numbness of fingers on both hands
Pain and numbness of the right leg
Pain in his shoulders with a feeling of great weight upon them when he over-exerts himself or sits/stands for long periods
Loss of sensation in both hands and his right foot
Difficulty in controlling fine movements of the hands
Morning stiffness: sometimes takes several minutes to uncurl his hands
Cannot stoop to pick things up; can only squat
Unable to resume his former employment in the electronic industry in a skilled supervisory or assistant managerial capacity (substantial permanent loss of employment claimed)

treatments_future: intensive course of physiotherapy for about 7 months including one month in hospital
surgical decompression of the spine followed by further physiotherapy

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Denied the swimming, ball games and hiking he used to enjoy

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Requires the services of a servant to do general housework
Unable to resume his former employment in the electronic industry in a skilled supervisory or assistant managerial capacity; substantial permanent loss of employment (as claimed)

comparable_cases.injury_description: "whiplash" injuries to the spine; injuries and suffering much more severe than in this case
